title: kv-cache-attn-kernel-seqlen-debug-scratchpad-13
content:
Context:
- Investigating intermittent token corruption and repeat tokens when requests straddle certain sequence length boundaries. Seen in hosted tests and locally with debug client. Suspect interaction between kv cache indexing and attention kernel selection when seq_len > tile boundary or equals power-of-two boundary (e.g., 2048, 4096).

Repro summary (observed):
- Model: redwood/open-7b-v2-ish (quantized prod-ish build)
- Config: chunked KV caching enabled, continuous batching on, kernel selection auto (flash-attn when supported else tiled)
- Input pattern: prompt length ~1200 tokens, then user message 900-1200 tokens so total past + new crosses 2048 boundary
- Symptom: generation sometimes repeats last 32-64 tokens or emits garbled tokens; other runs produce clean outputs

Steps to reproduce (local):
1) Start local serving runtime with debug flags:
   export DEBUG_KV_INDEX=1
   export DEBUG_KERNEL_SELECT=1
   ./scripts/run_local_runtime.sh --config tests/configs/kv-edgecase.yaml &

2) Run reproducer client (shortened):
   python -m tests.reproducers.kv_seqlen_repro --model open-7b-v2 --prompt tests/data/long_prompt_1200.txt --gen-len 800 --seed 42

Commands/traces I ran:
- run with kernel forced to tiled:
  ./bin/serve --force-kernel=tiled --model-path /mnt/models/open-7b-v2
  ==> result: no repeats across 30 runs (makes kernel selection a suspect)

- run with kernel forced to flash-attn:
  ./bin/serve --force-kernel=flash-attn --model-path /mnt/models/open-7b-v2
  ==> result: repeat observed in ~40% of runs

- run with kv-cache disabled:
  ./bin/serve --disable-kv-cache
  ==> result: no repeats (performance low but stable)

Relevant debug logs (abridged):
- When repeat occurs:
  [kv_cache] idx_write: 2047 -> 2048 (wrap boundary)
  [kv_cache] saved_kv_offset mismatch: expected 2048, got 2056
  [kernel_select] picked: flash-attn (seq_len=2056)
  [attention] computed qk indices: start=16 end=2064
  [generate] token 512 repeat detected, rollback triggered

- When stable run:
  [kv_cache] idx_write: 2047 -> 2048
  [kv_cache] saved_kv_offset: 2048
  [kernel_select] picked: tiled (seq_len=2048)
  [attention] computed qk indices: start=0 end=2048

Hypotheses:
1) Kernel selection decision uses observed seq_len after adding prompt+new tokens, but kv cache write uses block-aligned offsets; when kernel selection switches to a different tiling strategy (flash-attn expects contiguous KV layout), the runtime uses an offset that is off-by-block (e.g., kv pointer advanced by pad or temp buffer) causing misaligned reads into KV cache. This leads to stale/shifted keys and repeated outputs.
2) There's a race between KV cache flush/commit and kernel chooser when continuous batching merges requests of different seq lengths. If one request causes a boundary transition, the chosen kernel for the batch may not match the kernel expected by the per-request KV layout.
3) Numeric overflow/clip in seq_len accounting when using 16-bit counters for large multi-chunk sequences (less likely but worth checking).

Quick checks I ran:
- Dumped raw KV indices before/after kernel selection in both kernels. Observed an off-by-8 or off-by-16 difference aligning with PCIe page size? (could be coincidence).
- Added assertion in kv cache writer: assert(saved_kv_offset % kv_block_size == 0). This fired in failing runs.
- Re-ran with smaller batch size and continuous batching off: failures drop to <5%.

Reproducer script notes (tests/reproducers/kv_seqlen_repro):
- builds prompt to trigger boundary: pad prompt until total tokens == kv_block_size - 8, then append user message of length 24 to cross boundary by small amount
- seeds PRNG to make generation deterministic; reproduces ~70% locally when running with flash-attn

Potential fixes to try next (ordered):
1) Make kernel selection deterministic per-request before KV write/commit. Ensure kernel decision is based on per-request padded seq_len and that KV writer writes with the same padding semantics.
2) Tighten synchronization: hold KV mutex until kernel selection completes and kernel's expected layout is known. Evaluate perf cost.
3) Normalize saved_kv_offset to block alignment explicitly (round up) and ensure reads use normalized index. Add unit tests.
4) Add telemetry metric for saved_kv_offset mismatch count and attach to rollouts.

Local TODOs
- [ ] Add unit test in tests/unit/kv_cache to assert no offset mismatch across kernel choices.
- [ ] Instrument kernel_select to log chosen kernel + per-request expected layout in detail.
- [ ] Run internal canary with --force-kernel=tiled to confirm customer incidence drops.
- [ ] Run fuzzing on boundary values (kv_block_size +/- [0..128]) and log mismatch distribution.
- [ ] Check GPU memory allocator for small alignment rounding that might cause off-by-8/16 artifacts.

Notes to Miguel/Lena:
- Miguel: see linked PR 482 for recent changes to flash-attn layout optimization; I think the prefetch buffer change might be related.
- Lena: can you add a metric in console for saved_kv_offset_mismatch? We should make it visible for Dedicated customers.

Scratch/debug commands history (for quick paste):
- ./bin/serve --force-kernel=flash-attn --log-level=debug 2>&1 | tee /tmp/kv-flash-debug.log
- python -m tests.reproducers.kv_seqlen_repro --model open-7b-v2 --prompt tests/data/long_prompt_1200.txt --gen-len 800 --seed 42 --log /tmp/repro.log
- git checkout -b fix/kv-offset-align
- # temporary assertion enabled in kv_cache_writer.cpp
- pytest tests/unit/test_kv_cache.py::test_block_alignment -q

Recent cliff notes:
- Kernel choice matters in repro (flash-attn more likely to fail).
- KV offset mismatch shows up in logs before misgen.
- Disabling kv-cache or forcing tiled kernel avoids issue.

If I get time this week: implement quick normalization of saved_kv_offset (round up to block), run canary with increased logging and see if occurrence rate drops. If it does, followup with proper fix and add unit tests.

References:
- linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/482
- internal ticket: RED-913
- slack thread: https://slack.com/archives/C02ABCD123/p1670000000000000
